name: APP-scam / instant-payments risk
parent_research_topic: Beava's current market position — competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against

competitive_landscape.incumbents: The generic infra layer underneath every named fraud vendor in this segment is the same stack beava sets out to replace: Redis (Enterprise/Cluster) with Lua scripts for online counters (one major card network publicly cited ~700k TPS scoring on Redis), Apache Flink / Kafka Streams for windowed aggregates, Aerospike as the low-latency feature serving store (PayPal, Forter migrated from Redis-and-Couchbase to Aerospike for ~10x p99 improvement; Caulis migrated for scale), and Kafka as the universal ingress. Feature-store overlays on top — Tecton (now Databricks-owned), Chalk, Feast, Hopsworks, Fennel (now Databricks-owned) — exist but are not the live decisioning store at most banks; the live store is still Redis-or-Aerospike. Streaming SQL (Materialize-BSL, RisingWave-Apache-2.0, ksqlDB) shows up in scams-and-AML PoCs but rarely in the synchronous decision path. The 'DIY pattern' (Kafka + Flink + Redis/Aerospike + an external scorer) is the architecture every named vendor below is trying to abstract over.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The named APP-scam / instant-payments-risk vendors are: (1) Featurespace ARIC Scam Detect — acquired by Visa Dec 2024, now relaunched Feb 2026 as 'Visa A2A Protect', a single Visa-network risk-scoring API; in Pay.UK PoC the models detected up to 33% of previously missed scams and contributed to $200M loss reduction; protects ~500M consumers, processes ~100B payments/year. (2) Feedzai — $75M raise Oct 2025 pushed valuation above $2B, protects ~1B consumers, processes ~$8B/yr, AI-native RiskOps. (3) NICE Actimize IFM-X — purpose-built for FedNow/RTP, sub-ms response, 2025 NICE Actimize Fraud Insights report names scams as the dominant attempted-fraud method. (4) Hawk AI — $56M Series C April 2025 (One Peak led; brings total funding to $134M+); 80+ Tier-1-to-mid-market customers; rail-agnostic, API-driven, pre-settlement interdiction. (5) ThreatMetrix (LexisNexis Risk Solutions) — 110M daily auth/trust decisions across 1.4B tokenized identities; bank deployment cited 60% scam detection / 80% ATO / 80% mule. (6) ComplyAdvantage — ~$88M raised to date, real-time sanctions/PEP/adverse-media, transaction monitoring claims 70% false-positive reduction. (7) BioCatch Scams360 — behavioral biometrics for social-engineering-in-progress detection, $160M ARR June 2025; Q3 2025 network processed 180M payments / $330B / surfaced $60M attempted fraud. (8) Sardine — $70M Series C Feb 2025 (Activant led, $145M total), 130% YoY ARR growth, 2.2B devices profiled, 300+ enterprise customers. (9) Flagright — sub-half-second API in production, #1 G2 Transaction Monitoring Summer 2025, AI-native AML for payment processors. (10) Bank-side network/consortium plays: Mastercard Consumer Fraud Risk (9-UK-bank consortium incl. Lloyds, NatWest, Monzo), Pay.UK RCMS (compliance May 2025). None of these are sold as a developer-facing feature server — they bundle ingestion, behavioral biometrics, network intelligence, models, case management, and analytics behind a closed API.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Dominantly proprietary. Featurespace/Visa A2A Protect, Feedzai, NICE Actimize, Hawk AI, ThreatMetrix, BioCatch, Sardine, Flagright, ComplyAdvantage are all closed-source SaaS or appliance. OSS challengers exist but are narrow: Marble (Apache-2.0 self-host option, decision engine — not a feature store), Tazama (Gates-Foundation-backed Apache-2.0 transaction monitoring for emerging markets). Underlying infra is mixed: Redis-OSS post-AGPL re-license vs Valkey (cloud-default Apache-2.0), Aerospike (proprietary core + community edition), Flink/Kafka (Apache-2.0). Beava's Apache-2.0, no-open-core posture is a real wedge against the BSL Redis-8 fork and against any bank refusing mixed-license stacks for regulator review.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium. The hyperscaler bundle today is 'Databricks (post-Tecton/Fennel) feature platform + your own scorer' or 'Redis Cloud Feature Form (post-Featureform acq Oct 2025) + your own scorer' — these are credible for the offline-feature / batch-scoring half of a fraud stack but they are not yet the live sub-100ms decisioning store for a regulated payment rail. Stripe Radar AI is a closed-loop competitor but locks customers to Stripe payment flows, so it does not threaten bank-rail APP-scam decisioning. The bigger 'bundle' threat is Visa itself: with Featurespace integrated as Visa A2A Protect (13-field plug-and-play API), Visa is effectively offering APP-scam risk as a network service to every issuer — a buyer can get a 'good enough' answer without building anything. That is a category-collapse threat similar to what Stripe Radar did to e-commerce CNP. For non-Visa rails (FedNow, RTP, SEPA Instant non-card, UPI), this threat is lower and beava-class self-host stays attractive.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Upstream producers expected by buyers: payment switch / orchestrator (push via vendor-specific message bus, gRPC, or HTTP to the scoring engine), ISO 20022 pacs.008/pacs.002 from FedLine/FedNow API, RTP API, EBA RT1/TIPS/SEPA Instant CSMs, NPCI UPI Switch; CoP/VoP lookup services (Pay.UK CoP, EPC VoP scheme rulebook in force Oct 5 2025); behavioural session collectors from mobile/web SDKs (BioCatch/ThreatMark-style); sanctions/PEP feeds (ComplyAdvantage, Refinitiv, LSEG). Most named feature stores expect Kafka as the only ingress (Feast, Tecton, Hopsworks, Fennel/Databricks). Beava's HTTP/TCP-push model is a good fit for the bank's existing payment-orchestrator-to-scorer pattern (the orchestrator already speaks HTTP/REST) but is a friction point with Kafka-first reference architectures published by SEPA-Instant integrators (EY, Oliver Wyman, Linkurious). A thin Kafka-to-beava-TCP sidecar closes this; gRPC support would close the recognised gap with Tecton/Chalk for the fraud-platform vendors who want to embed beava.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Production stacks always run a deterministic rules engine (Drools, in-house DSL, or the vendor's rule language — e.g. Featurespace's rules layer, Hawk's explainable AI overlay) alongside one or more ML scorers (XGBoost, LightGBM, increasingly graph-neural / sequence models for mule rings). Regulators (FCA SYSC, EU IPR Art 5d, RBI/NPCI) expect explainable rule paths. Beava's role is upstream of both — it serves the feature vector; the rules and models live in the bank's scoring service or the vendor's closed-box scorer.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Single binary, Apache-2.0, no broker required, with 50+ aggregation primitives that map 1:1 to the APP-scam / instant-payments feature shapes: per-payer + per-(payer,counterparty) + per-counterparty velocity counters, first-time-payee flags, amount z-scores and percentile-ranks, distinct-counterparty HLL, inbound-mule fan-in counts, and sub-100ms batch_get for the 50–200 features a typical scorer reads per payment. Published ~684k EPS single-M4-core (TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) is 2 orders of magnitude above a tier-1 UK bank's outbound rate (~15–50 EPS sustained, peak low-thousands) and gives multi-x headroom even after the 10–30x read amplification per decision. Atomic per-event update-and-read fits the regulator-graded 'feature value at decision time must reflect this event' requirement that pure cache-of-precomputed-features stacks struggle with. The (payer, counterparty) pair grain — awkward in Redis+Lua and slow in a generic SQL feature store — is a first-class `@bv.table(key=(payer,counterparty))` declaration in beava. Apache-2.0 with no open-core matters specifically for (a) regulated buyers reviewing license posture as part of vendor risk, and (b) fraud-platform vendors (Hawk, Flagright, Sardine, ComplyAdvantage, regional regtechs) who want to embed beava without per-decision license fees. Sub-second WAL durability and 'refuse on network-FS' guardrail are the right defaults for the regulator-grade durability bar (AML/BSA, EU IPR, UK PSR PS25/5, FCA SYSC).
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Production-blocking, in roughly decreasing priority: (1) No TLS on the wire and no authentication on :8080/:8081/:8090 admin — instant rejection by any UK/EU bank or regulated PSP; (2) No authn/authz / no RBAC / no per-tenant namespaces — every regulated buyer requires this, fraud-platform vendors embedding beava need multi-tenancy; (3) No in-process sharding and no replication / failover — a tier-1 bank cannot run live payment scoring on a single failure-domain node (UK FCA operational-resilience and EU DORA both expect dual-region capability), and the long-tail (payer,counterparty) pair space at tier-1 scale (~1.5B pairs / ~150GB+) is awkward on a single node; (4) In-memory only with WAL+periodic snapshot — fraud teams are nervous about losing 30–90-day behavioural baselines on a crash even with WAL replay, want hot-standby + synchronous WAL streaming; (5) No triggers / no event-driven actions — APP detection wants 'fire when velocity crosses threshold' to step-up to face-biometric / hand off to call-back queue, today the caller must poll; (6) No per-decision feature-snapshot export (a signed, compact record of every feature value seen by the scorer at decision time) — required for PSR/FOS replay under the Oct-2024 mandatory-reimbursement regime; (7) No at-rest encryption — account numbers, sort codes, msisdns are PII, GDPR/DPDP-Act-mandatory; (8) No native sanctions-list / PEP-list join or 'is_sanctioned' precomputed flag surface — EU IPR Art 5d explicitly moved sanctions to daily-full-base screening, so a precomputed flag is the right shape; (9) No first-class session-window semantics with idle-timeout for behavioral signals (typing pauses, copy-paste, sensor-proximity) — must be modelled with explicit session keys today; (10) No multi-tenancy for fraud-platform vendors that want to embed beava across many bank customers; (11) No time-travel / 'as-of' reads for regulator replay; (12) No graph features for mule-ring detection (Linkurious, TigerGraph, Quantexa cover this gap); (13) No native CoP/VoP enrichment helper as a first-class event type; (14) v0 events-only / processing-time-only — pacs.008 timestamps cannot be used as event time, which is acceptable for live decisioning but blocks some 'as-of-event-time' regulator queries.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo. TLS+auth (~1mo), per-decision feature-snapshot export (~1mo), at-rest encryption (~0.5mo), triggers/webhooks (~1–2mo), replication+failover (~2–3mo), sharding (~3+mo). Demoable 'beava + synthetic FPS / pacs.008 traffic + XGBoost scorer' is already weeks-away; sellable into a tier-1 UK/EU bank is the 6-12mo bar driven by TLS+auth+replication+audit-grade snapshot export.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: No public beava deployment, case study, or design-partner announcement for APP-scam / instant-payments risk as of May 2026. No examples/app_fraud/ or examples/instant_payments/ vertical demo currently in the repo (per use-case 1b and 1c filesystem checks; both flagged as uncertain). No beava-specific GitHub Issues, Discord threads, or RFC discussions on APP scams have surfaced in public search. The buyer is well known (Head of Payment Risk / Head of Fraud at a bank or PSP; ML / data-platform team as technical sponsor) — beava knows who buys but has no proof points yet. Comparable platforms have abundant proof: Featurespace at NatWest (135% scam detection lift, 75% FP reduction), ClearBank, HSBC; Feedzai at Citi, Standard Chartered, Lloyds; NICE Actimize across FedNow/RTP participants; BioCatch Scams360 surfacing $60M attempted fraud in Q3 2025 alone; Sardine at FIS, Ascensus, Deel; Mastercard Consumer Fraud Risk consortium across 9 UK banks. The validation gap is the central risk for this segment. [uncertain]
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete. Strongest 12-month regulatory tailwind of any beava segment (EU IPR + VoP Oct 9 2025 already live for Eurozone, July 9 2027 for non-Euro EU; UK PSR mandatory reimbursement live since Oct 7 2024 with 88% of stolen funds returned and £173M paid in first year; FedNow $10M limit live Nov 12 2025 unlocking corporate-treasury rails; SEPA Instant mandatory send Oct 9 2025; AU SPF Feb 2025; SG SRF Dec 16 2024). Beava's data-model fit is excellent — the pair-grain, velocity-counter, first-time-payee, batch-get-50-features primitives map directly. But the disqualifier list (TLS/auth/sharding/replication/feature-snapshot-export) is non-trivial AND the Visa-A2A-Protect category-collapse threat is real for Visa-attached issuers. Best play is design-partner motion at a challenger bank / EMI / SEPA-Instant-PSP at the smaller end of the regulator-driven scramble (where one-node-on-a-beefy-box is actually fine and TLS+auth is enough), plus an embed-partner motion with a mid-sized AML vendor (Flagright, Hawk, ComplyAdvantage, regional regtech) who needs a feature backend they can self-host across their customer base.
